To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Firewall policy can be analyzed by using argumentation by adding the concept of “arguments” and “reasons” to firewall rules”.

the use of argumentation can help in the analysis of firewall policy, that the resulting framework can help in the detection of anomalies, that the use of reasons can be helpful in providing better recommendations to resolve the detected anomalies, and that the framework can be useful as an educational tool.

(1) the new framework is a useful addition to the existing approaches for firewall policy analysis; (2) it is possible to identify new anomalies in a policy that cannot be identified by existing approaches; (3) the new approach is more flexible than existing approaches, and (4) the new approach can also be used to give recommendations on how to resolve the detected anomalies.

the following question: how can we use the argumentation framework to analyze firewall policies?
how argumentation can be used to improve the quality of firewall policies.

the following questions: (1) How to model firewall policy as argumentation? (2) How to identify anomalies in firewall policy? (3) What is the best way of resolving those anomalies? (4) How to evaluate the proposed framework?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this new framework is a promising approach for firewall policy analysis and, in particular, for anomaly detection and resolution.
this paper presents a framework for firewall policy analysis that can be used to find anomalies and provide suggestions for fixing the anomalies.
the proposed framework provides an interesting new way to analyze and reason about firewall policies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a new way to analyze firewall policies by introducing a new framework that is based on the idea of arguing about reasons, instead of arguing about firewall rules.

, we have shown that it is possible to extend the traditional rule based firewall policy with reasons and argue about them, and that this extension is useful for identifying anomalies and for giving stronger recommendations to resolve them.
, by using arguments, it is possible to analyze a firewall policy in a much more fine-grained way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of reasons can be used to design new frameworks for analyzing firewall policy.
the firewall policy can be analyzed in a way that is much closer to the way a firewall expert does it.
, in the context of firewall policy analysis, it makes sense to reason about the reasons, and not the firewall rules.
